title: Run independent plan-group items in parallel in the drain loop
summary: Reading: the drain loop (crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs) plans items into parallel groups (`plan_groups`) but runs one job at a time; build the first parallel slice so items of one plan group run concurrently, bounded by a worker limit, following docs/design/parallel-jobs.md (child-process model, per-job locks and budgets, kill switch). Audience: the Athena user running a drain, who wants shorter wall time without weakened gates.

defaults_applied.how: New tests for concurrency, bound, isolation, kill switch; cargo test and clippy clean.
Behavior criteria name cargo commands the verifier can run.
Criteria check items actually overlapping, not that types exist.
One focused slice: drain-group concurrency only.
Kill switch and bound enforced in code and tested.
Docs and comments written for outside readers.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: 'The plan's groups' means Report::plan_groups / Plan::groups in drain.rs and plan.rs, whose docs call concurrent group running 'follow-up work'.
The first build is the drain-loop slice, not the full multi-job `athena go a b c`/`--all` launcher with --pr phase from the design's section 10 item 4.

Concurrency is built to the design's recommendation (processes or isolation without Send/Sync changes to AgentDriver/Ui) unless the drain's Steps abstraction allows a simpler safe approach; worker default 2, ceiling 4 as the design states.
README, CHANGELOG and decisions.md entries belong to a later docs job per the design, so they are not expected to change.
Default worker bound keeps current behavior safe; exact default is the producer's call within the design's 2/4.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new test in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs drives the drain with a fake Steps whose jobs block on a barrier; with a bound of 2 and two independent items in one plan group, both are in flight at once (the test fails if run serially). Run `cargo test -p athena-cli`.

A test shows the worker bound is respected: with a bound of 1 (or more items than workers) no more than the bound run at once, and items in later groups start only after the earlier group's items finish. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli`.
A test shows one item's failure or refusal does not abort siblings in its group, and that turning the kill switch (Stop) on mid-run starts no further item. Run `cargo test`.

With the bound at 1 or the default, the existing drain tests still pass unchanged: serial order, report and exit codes for single-job `athena go` are unchanged. Run `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` (clean) and `cargo fmt --check`.

Items that name no touched path or share a path stay serialized as plan.rs groups them; landing is still through the repository lock so nothing lands unverified; any new setting (worker bound, default and ceiling) is documented where it is defined.

The drain's module docs and the Report no longer say the loop runs one job at a time; the design doc's status or build plan notes what this slice built and what remains (multi-job `athena go`, --pr phase). Any change to athena.toml is named here and justified.

out_of_scope: Automatic merging or re-verification of stale jobs
departures: Concurrency across the drain, locks and kill switch is larger and riskier than a typical change, and the request is ambiguous between the drain slice and the full launcher, so costs are higher and pass odds lower than the reference.
